newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Flemish investors can take Tractebel stake - SGB.
newsitem.headline: Flemish investors can take Tractebel stake - SGB.

text.p: Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique (SGB) said in a statement that it plans to propose a number of changes to the management structure of its unit Tractebel, which will clear the way for Flemish private investors to take a stake in Tractebel.
An SGB spokesman told Reuters on Tuesday that investors will have to buy their Tractebel shares on the bourse, not from SGB.
"We are not willing to sell our shares. The private investors are aware of this and have agreed to this," he said.
The spokesman declined to say who the investors are and what the size of their stake could be.

The SGB statement said that at the Tractebel board meeting of March 18, SGB will propose the nomination of Anton Dieusaert, vice chairman of the Flemish Employers Federation (VEV) and CEO of BASF Antwerp as an independent board member.
Dieusaert will also become member of a strategic committee in the board.

"With these proposals the management of SGB and Tractebel again underline their firm commitment to bring Tractebel's strategy and management in line with Belgium's federal structure," the SGB statement said.
SGB has a 65 percent stake in utility group Tractebel.

In recent years, Tractebel has run into political opposition when it wanted to expand in utility services in Flanders. Some politicians and media in Dutch-speaking Flanders consider the SGB group -- owned 62 percent by Compagnie de Suez -- too French.
